documents.title: zerolog — Zero Allocation JSON Logger
documents.description: Fast, simple structured logging for Go, dedicated to JSON output. Leveled logging, sampling, hooks, contextual fields, and a chaining API that avoids allocations and reflection.
documents.searchText: # zerolog {#zerolog} the package provides a fast and simple logger dedicated to json output. zerolog's api is designed provide both great developer experience stunning performance. its unique chaining allows write (or cbor) log events by avoiding allocations reflection. uber's [zap](https://godoc.org/go.uber.org/zap) library pioneered this approach. takes concept next level with simpler use even better keep code base simple, focuses on efficient structured logging only. pretty console made possible using provided (but inefficient) `zerolog.consolewriter`. ## what you get {#what-you-get} - **blazing fast, low zero allocation** — see [performance](/zerolog/guides/performance.html). **leveled logging** trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal, panic, plus global switch. **log sampling** `basicsampler` `burstsampler` high-volume debug output under control. **hooks** run every event, for example attach severity or trace id. **contextual fields** strongly typed key/value pairs, sub-loggers, `context.context` integration. **integration `net/http`** `hlog` carries through request handlers. **json cbor encoding** binary logs via `binary_log` build tag. **pretty development** `consolewriter` turns into colorized lines. **error optional stacktrace** `github.com/pkg/errors` `pkgerrors.marshalstack`. **`log/slog` integration** `slog.handler` that routes standard-library records zerolog. where start {#where-to-start} new zerolog? read [quickstart](/zerolog/quickstart.html) install, your first line, leveled event. already logging? [levels sampling](/zerolog/guides/levels-sampling.html) [context fields](/zerolog/guides/context-fields.html) cover daily api. shipping production? [writers output](/zerolog/guides/writers-output.html) [performance](/zerolog/guides/performance.html) outputs, diode writer, caveats bite (field duplication, `event` pooling, `updatecontext` concurrency). reference {#api-reference} [go api](/zerolog/api.html) tab full `github.com/rs/zerolog` package, generated from source: 26 types, 20 package-level functions, 215 methods, 16 constants, 34 variables including `logger`, `event`, `context`, `consolewriter`, `multilevelwriter`, samplers. documented version {#documented-version} site documents **rs/zerolog @ 284f7c8** (commit `284f7c889533b78603191349f4a5c48628d7afd2`, 10 nov 2026), mit licensed. source links in point at exact commit github.

documents.title: Quickstart
documents.description: Install zerolog, write your first log line, and log your first leveled event with contextual fields.
documents.searchText: # quickstart {#quickstart} ## install {#install} ```bash go get -u github.com/rs/zerolog/log ``` your first log line {#your-first-log-line} for simple logging, import the global logger package `github.com/rs/zerolog/log`: ```go main ( "github.com/rs/zerolog" "github.com/rs/zerolog/log" ) func main() { // unix time is faster and smaller than most timestamps zerolog.timefieldformat = zerolog.timeformatunix log.print("hello world") } output: {"time":1516134303,"level":"debug","message":"hello world"} by default `log` writes to `os.stderr`. level `log.print` *trace*. leveled event {#your-first-leveled-event} log.info().msg("hello {"time":1516134303,"level":"info","message":"hello it very important note that when using chaining api, as shown above (`log.info().msg("hello world")`), chain must have either `msg` or `msgf` method call. if you forget add of these, will not occur there no compile error alert this. contextual fields {#add-contextual-fields} zerolog allows data be added messages in form key:value pairs. message adds "context" about can critical debugging well myriad other purposes: log.debug(). str("scale", "833 cents"). float64("interval", 833.09). msg("fibonacci everywhere") str("name", "tom"). send() {"level":"debug","scale":"833 cents","interval":833.09,"time":1562212768,"message":"fibonacci everywhere"} {"level":"debug","name":"tom","time":1562212768} example adding fields, are strongly typed. full list supported field types [go api](/zerolog/api.html) reference under `event` — `str`, `bool`, `int`, `int64`, `float64`, `dur`, `dict`, `err`, `time`, more, them also slice (`strs`, `errs`, so on). create own {#create-your-own-logger} := zerolog.new(os.stderr).with().timestamp().logger() logger.info().str("foo", "bar").msg("hello {"level":"info","time":1494567715,"message":"hello world","foo":"bar"} sub-loggers let loggers with additional context: sublogger log.with(). str("component", "foo"). logger() sublogger.info().msg("hello world","component":"foo"} next steps {#next-steps} - [levels sampling](/zerolog/guides/levels-sampling.html) seven levels, switch, sampling. [context fields](/zerolog/guides/context-fields.html) sub-loggers, hooks, caller info, names. [writers output](/zerolog/guides/writers-output.html) console output, multiple outputs, non-blocking diode writer.

documents.title: Levels and sampling
documents.description: The seven log levels, the global level switch, logging without a level, and sampling with BasicSampler and BurstSampler.
documents.searchText: # levels and sampling {#levels-and-sampling} ## the {#the-levels} zerolog allows for logging at following (from highest to lowest): - panic (`zerolog.paniclevel`, 5) fatal (`zerolog.fatallevel`, 4) error (`zerolog.errorlevel`, 3) warn (`zerolog.warnlevel`, 2) info (`zerolog.infolevel`, 1) debug (`zerolog.debuglevel`, 0) trace (`zerolog.tracelevel`, -1) setting global level {#setting-the-global-level} you can set any of these options using `setgloballevel` function in package, passing one given constants above, e.g. `zerolog.infolevel` would be "info" level. whichever is chosen, all logs with a greater than or equal that will written. turn off entirely, pass `zerolog.disabled` constant. if never call `setgloballevel`, logger writes `os.stderr` `trace` (the lowest level), so **every** event — `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `fatal`, `panic` written stderr by default. calling `zerolog.setgloballevel(zerolog.infolevel)` raises minimum `debug` messages are suppressed. this example uses command-line flags demonstrate various outputs depending on chosen log level: ```go package main import ( "flag" "github.com/rs/zerolog" "github.com/rs/zerolog/log" ) func main() { zerolog.timefieldformat = zerolog.timeformatunix := flag.bool("debug", false, "sets debug") flag.parse() // default info, unless flag present zerolog.setgloballevel(zerolog.infolevel) *debug zerolog.setgloballevel(zerolog.debuglevel) } log.debug().msg("this message appears only when log.info().msg("this info") e log.debug(); e.enabled() compute output enabled. value "bar" e.str("foo", value).msg("some message") ``` (no flag): ```bash $ ./loglevelexample {"time":1516387492,"level":"info","message":"this info"} (debug set): -debug {"time":1516387573,"level":"debug","message":"this debug"} {"time":1516387573,"level":"info","message":"this {"time":1516387573,"level":"debug","foo":"bar","message":"some message"} without {#logging-without-a-level-or-message} may choose specific `log` method. also write an empty string `msg string` parameter `msg` method: log.log(). str("foo", "bar"). msg("") output: {"time":1494567715,"foo":"bar"} {#error-and-fatal-logging} errors `err` "errors" err errors.new("seems we have here") log.error().err(err).msg("") {"level":"error","error":"seems here","time":1609085256} field name `error`; change `zerolog.errorfieldname` meet your needs. exits process status 1 after writing: errors.new("a repo man spends his life getting into tense situations") service "myservice" log.fatal(). err(err). str("service", service). msgf("cannot start %s", service) {"time":1516133263,"level":"fatal","error":"a situations","service":"myservice","message":"cannot myservice"} exit note: `msgf` generates allocation even disabled. ### stacktrace {#error-logging-with-a-stacktrace} `github.com/pkg/errors`, add formatted errors: "github.com/pkg/errors" "github.com/rs/zerolog/pkgerrors" zerolog.errorstackmarshaler pkgerrors.marshalstack outer() log.error().stack().err(err).msg("") `zerolog.errorstackmarshaler` must order stack anything. see `pkgerrors.marshalstack` [go api](/zerolog/api.html) reference. {#log-sampling} sampled log.sample(&zerolog.basicsampler{n: 10}) sampled.info().msg("will logged every 10 messages") {"time":1494567715,"level":"info","message":"will messages"} more advanced sampling: let 5 per period second. over message, 100 logged. other not sampled. log.sample(zerolog.levelsampler{ debugsampler: &zerolog.burstsampler{ burst: 5, period: 1*time.second, nextsampler: &zerolog.basicsampler{n: 100}, }, }) sampled.debug().msg("hello world") {"time":1494567715,"level":"debug","message":"hello world"} controlled `logger.sample`, globally `zerolog.disablesampling` `true`, loggers stop issue 100% their events.

documents.searchText: # context and fields {#context-and-fields} ## field types {#field-types} ### standard {#standard-types} - `str` `bool` `int`, `int8`, `int16`, `int32`, `int64` `uint`, `uint8`, `uint16`, `uint32`, `uint64` `float32`, `float64` advanced {#advanced-fields} `err`: takes an `error` renders it as a string using the `zerolog.errorfieldname` name. `func`: run `func` only if level is enabled. `timestamp`: inserts timestamp with `zerolog.timestampfieldname` name, formatted `zerolog.timefieldformat`. `time`: adds time `dur`: `time.duration`. `dict`: sub-key/value of event. `rawjson`: already encoded json (`[]byte`). `hex`: value hexadecimal `interface`: uses reflection to marshal type. `ipaddr`: `net.ip`. `ipprefix`: `net.ipnet`. `macaddr`: `net.hardwareaddr`. most are also available in slice format (`strs` for `[]string`, `errs` `[]error`, etc.). full list on `event` [go api](/zerolog/api.html) reference. sub-dictionary {#sub-dictionary} ```go log.info(). str("foo", "bar"). dict("dict", zerolog.dict(). str("bar", "baz"). int("n", 1), ).msg("hello world") // output: {"level":"info","time":1494567715,"foo":"bar","dict":{"bar":"baz","n":1},"message":"hello world"} ``` customize automatic names {#customize-automatic-field-names} zerolog.timestampfieldname = "t" zerolog.levelfieldname "l" zerolog.messagefieldname "m" log.info().msg("hello {"l":"info","t":1494567715,"m":"hello add contextual global logger {#add-contextual-fields-to-the-global-logger} log.logger log.with().str("foo", "bar").logger() file line number {#add-file-and-line-number} equivalent `llongfile`: log.with().caller().logger() {"level": "info", "message": "hello world", "caller": "/go/src/your_project/some_file:21"} `lshortfile`: zerolog.callermarshalfunc func(pc uintptr, string, int) { return filepath.base(file) + ":" strconv.itoa(line) } "some_file:21"} hooks {#hooks} type severityhook struct{} func (h severityhook) run(e *zerolog.event, zerolog.level, msg string) != zerolog.nolevel e.str("severity", level.string()) hooked := log.hook(severityhook{}) hooked.warn().msg("") {"level":"warn","severity":"warn"} hook runs every event its logger. `hookfunc` function form same interface; `logger.hook` attaches logger, can read event's `e.getctx()` — useful log trace span ids stored `context.context`. see [integrations](/zerolog/guides/integrations.html) tracing example. pass sub-logger by {#pass-a-sub-logger-by-context} ctx log.with().str("component", "module").logger().withcontext(ctx) log.ctx(ctx).info().msg("hello {"component":"module","level":"info","message":"hello context.context integration {#contextcontext-integration} go contexts commonly passed throughout code, this help you your into places might otherwise be hard inject. `logger` instance may attached (`context.context`) `logger.withcontext(ctx)` extracted from `zerolog.ctx(ctx)`: f() zerolog.new(os.stdout) context.background() attach logger.withcontext(ctx) somefunc(ctx) somefunc(ctx context.context) get context. it's nil, then `zerolog.defaultcontextlogger` returned, `defaultcontextlogger` disabled returned. zerolog.ctx(ctx) logger.info().msg("hello") second `context.context` allows current logged event, retrieve hooks. or other information context, facilitates unification logging some systems: tracinghook tracinghook) e.getctx() spanid getspanidfromcontext(ctx) per framework e.str("span-id", spanid) setup logger.hook(tracinghook{}) use make logger.info().ctx(ctx).msg("hello") settings {#global-settings} changed will applied all loggers: `log.logger`: set (the one used package methods). `zerolog.setgloballevel`: raise minimum loggers. call `zerolog.disabled` disable altogether (quiet mode). `zerolog.disablesampling`: argument `true`, sampled loggers stop sampling issue 100% their events. `zerolog.timestampfieldname`: `timestamp` `zerolog.levelfieldname`: `zerolog.messagefieldname`: message `zerolog.errorfieldname`: `err` `zerolog.timefieldformat`: `time` formatting. `zerolog.timeformatunix`, `zerolog.timeformatunixms` `zerolog.timeformatunixmicro`, times unix timestamps. `zerolog.durationfieldunit`: unit `time.duration` added `dur` (default: `time.millisecond`). `zerolog.durationfieldformat`: `durationformatfloat`, `durationformatint`, `durationformatstring` `durationformatfloat`) append `duration` `float64`, `int64`, calling `string()` (respectively). `zerolog.errorhandler`: called whenever zerolog fails write output. not set, error printed stderr. handler must thread safe non-blocking. `zerolog.floatingpointprecision`: than -1, controls digits when formatting float numbers json. [strconv.formatfloat](https://pkg.go.dev/strconv#formatfloat) more details.

documents.title: Writers and output
documents.description: ConsoleWriter pretty logging, multiple outputs with MultiLevelWriter, the lock-free diode writer, and syslog and journald writers.
documents.searchText: # writers and output {#writers-and-output} a zerolog `logger` writes to any `io.writer`. `zerolog.new` takes the writer; global logger `os.stderr` by default. ## pretty logging {#pretty-logging} log human-friendly, colorized output, use `zerolog.consolewriter`: ```go log.logger = log.output(zerolog.consolewriter{out: os.stderr}) log.info().str("foo", "bar").msg("hello world") // output: 3:04pm inf hello world foo=bar ``` customize configuration formatting: := zerolog.consolewriter{out: os.stdout, timeformat: time.rfc3339} output.formatlevel func(i interface{}) string { return strings.toupper(fmt.sprintf("| %-6s|", i)) } output.formatmessage fmt.sprintf("***%s****", i) output.formatfieldname fmt.sprintf("%s:", output.formatfieldvalue strings.toupper(fmt.sprintf("%s", zerolog.new(output).with().timestamp().logger() 2006-01-02t15:04:05z07:00 | info ***hello world**** foo:bar custom advanced nocolor: true, partsorder: []string{"level", "one", "two", "three", "message"}, fieldsexclude: []string{"one", "three"}} strings.toupper(fmt.sprintf("%-6s", output.formatpartvaluebyname interface{}, s string) var ret switch case "one": "two": strings.tolower(fmt.sprintf("%s", "three": strings.tolower(fmt.sprintf("(%s)", zerolog.new(output) "bar"). str("two", "test_two"). str("one", "test_one"). str("three", "test_three"). msg("hello test_one test_two (test_three) console is for humans, not machines: it provided but inefficient writer. keep json anything pipeline will read. multiple outputs {#multiple-log-outputs} `zerolog.multilevelwriter` may be used send message outputs. in this example, we both `os.stdout` in-built `consolewriter`: func main() consolewriter os.stdout} multi zerolog.multilevelwriter(consolewriter, os.stdout) zerolog.new(multi).with().timestamp().logger() logger.info().msg("hello world!") (line 1: console; line 2: stdout) 12:36pm world! {"level":"info","time":"2019-11-07t12:36:38+03:00","message":"hello world!"} thread-safe, lock-free, non-blocking writer {#thread-safe-lock-free-non-blocking-writer} if your might slow or thread-safe you need producers never get slowed down writer, can `diode.writer` as follows: wr diode.newwriter(os.stdout, 1000, 10*time.millisecond, func(missed int) fmt.printf("logger dropped %d messages", missed) }) zerolog.new(wr) log.print("test") install `code.cloudfoundry.org/go-diodes` feature. diode drops messages when its buffer full reports count through callback — are blocked. syslog journald {#syslog-and-journald} package also ships system logging: `zerolog.sysloglevelwriter` syslog, `journald` subpackage systemd-journald. [go api](/zerolog/api.html) reference (`sysloglevelwriter`, separate module, covered site's root-package reference). binary encoding {#binary-encoding} addition default encoding, produce logs using [cbor](https://cbor.io) encoding. choice of decided at compile time build tag `binary_log` ```bash go -tags binary_log . decode encoded files cbor decoder. one that has been tested work with library [csd](https://github.com/toravir/csd/).

documents.title: Integrations
documents.description: Use zerolog with net/http via hlog, with the standard library log/slog, and as the standard logger's output.
documents.searchText: # integrations {#integrations} ## integration with `net/http` {#integration-with-nethttp} the `github.com/rs/zerolog/hlog` package provides some helpers to integrate zerolog `http.handler`. in this example we use [alice](https://github.com/justinas/alice) install logger for better readability: ```go log := zerolog.new(os.stdout).with(). timestamp(). str("role", "my-service"). str("host", host). logger() c alice.new() // handler default output on console = c.append(hlog.newhandler(log)) provided extra set request's context fields. thanks that handler, all our logs will come prepopulated c.append(hlog.accesshandler(func(r *http.request, status, size int, duration time.duration) { hlog.fromrequest(r).info(). str("method", r.method). stringer("url", r.url). int("status", status). int("size", size). dur("duration", duration). msg("") })) c.append(hlog.remoteaddrhandler("ip")) c.append(hlog.useragenthandler("user_agent")) c.append(hlog.refererhandler("referer")) c.append(hlog.requestidhandler("req_id", "request-id")) here is your final h c.then(http.handlerfunc(func(w http.responsewriter, r *http.request) get from context. you can safely assume it be always there: if removed, hlog.fromrequest return a no-op logger. str("user", "current user"). str("status", "ok"). msg("something happened") output: {"level":"info","time":"2001-02-03t04:05:06z","role":"my-service","host":"local-hostname","req_id":"b4g0l5t6tfid6dtrapu0","user":"current user","status":"ok","message":"something happened"} http.handle("/", h) err http.listenandserve(":8080", nil); != nil log.fatal().err(err).msg("startup failed") } ``` `log/slog` {#integration-with-logslog} `slog.handler` implementation routes records through lets standard library's `slog` api while keeping zerolog's performance and encoding: main import ( "log/slog" "github.com/rs/zerolog" "github.com/rs/zerolog/log" ) func main() zl log.logger zerolog.newsloghandler(zl) slog.new(handler) logger.info("user logged in", "user", "alice", "role", "admin") {"level":"info","user":"alice","role":"admin","time":"...","message":"user in"} supports features including `withattrs`, `withgroup`, nested groups, `logvaluer` resolution. slog levels are mapped (e.g. `slog.leveldebug` `zerolog.debuglevel`). as {#set-as-standard-logger-output} str("foo", "bar"). stdlog.setflags(0) stdlog.setoutput(log) stdlog.print("hello world") {"foo":"bar","message":"hello world"} related projects {#related-projects} - [grpc-zerolog](https://github.com/cheaproc/grpc-zerolog): of `grpclog.loggerv2` interface using zerolog. [overlog](https://github.com/trendyol/overlog): `mapped diagnostic context` [zerologr](https://github.com/go-logr/zerologr): `logr.logsink` [logze](https://github.com/maxbolgarin/logze):

documents.title: Performance
documents.description: Why zerolog is fast, the benchmark numbers, and the caveats to respect — field duplication, Event pooling, and UpdateContext concurrency.
documents.searchText: # performance {#performance} ## why it is fast {#why-it-is-fast} zerolog's chaining api writes json (or cbor) log events by avoiding allocations and reflection. that the whole design: a level method returns an `event`, field methods append directly to event's buffer, `msg`/`send` buffer once. disabled levels short-circuit before any work happens — guard expensive computation with `e.enabled()` when matters. see [logbench](http://bench.zerolog.io/) for more comprehensive up-to-date benchmarks. all operations are allocation free (those numbers *include* encoding): ```text benchmarklogempty-8 100000000 19.1 ns/op 0 b/op allocs/op benchmarkdisabled-8 500000000 4.07 benchmarkinfo-8 30000000 42.5 benchmarkcontextfields-8 44.9 benchmarklogfields-8 10000000 184 ``` using uber's zap comparison benchmark: message 10 fields: | library time bytes allocated objects :------------------ :---------: :-------------: :---------------: zerolog 767 552 6 848 704 2 (sugared) 1363 1610 20 go-kit 3614 2895 66 lion 5392 5807 63 logrus 5661 6092 78 apex/log 15332 3832 65 log15 20657 5632 93 logger already has fields of context: 52 283 337 80 2702 4074 38 3378 3046 14179 2642 44 static string, without context or `printf`-style templating: :--------: 50 236 standard 453 508 656 13 771 1224 1244 1505 27 2751 11 5181 1592 26 there few go logging benchmarks comparisons include zerolog: [imkira/go-loggers-bench](https://github.com/imkira/go-loggers-bench) [uber-go/zap](https://github.com/uber-go/zap#performance). caveats {#caveats} ### duplication {#field-duplication} note does no de-duplication fields. same key multiple times creates keys in final json: ```go := zerolog.new(os.stderr).with().timestamp().logger() logger.info(). timestamp(). msg("dup") // output: {"level":"info","time":1494567715,"time":1494567715,"message":"dup"} this case, many consumers will take last value, but not guaranteed; check yours if doubt. concurrency safety {#concurrency-safety} be careful calling `updatecontext`. safe. use `with()` create child logger: func handler(w http.responsewriter, r *http.request) { log.logger.with().logger() add fields, example user-agent from http headers logger.updatecontext(func(c zerolog.context) zerolog.context ... }) } do hold `array`, `dict` references {#do-not-hold-event-array-or-dict-references} `event` object returned `logger` level-specific functions (e.g. `log()`, `trace()`, `debug()`, etc.) `sync.pool` memory pool as soon `msg()`, `msgf()`, `send()`, `msgfunc()` **must not** accessed afterwards. **do reference `*event` while callback your own code. especially important `hook.run()` `hookfunc` `marshalzerologobject(e *event)` `logobjectmarshaler` implementations). `array` `context.createarray()` `event.createarray()` so them within `marshalzerologarray(a *array)` `logarraymarshaler` implementations) code they cleared after being buffered call `context.array()` `event.array()`. *dictionary* `context.createdict()` `event.createdict()` referenced `array.dict()`, `context.dict()`, `event.dict()` pool.
